text:
**Short answer: a roughly 1,000 Wh power station is the sweet spot, and I'd pick the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh).**

**Why it works**
- Electric blankets draw little power. The Department of Energy figures cited by [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/) are about 60 W for a single and 100 W for a double. Sunbeam rates its full-size blankets at 110 W. At 100 W, a 1,024 Wh unit runs the blanket for about 8 hours, which is roughly one night.
- [Blackout Wise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket) names the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 as its top pick. It says the 1,024 Wh battery runs a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours, so a full 8-hour night with some left over. It usually sells for about $380 to $500 and weighs 25 lb. Blackout Wise also says a queen blanket cycles on and off and averages about 75 W, so [a 1,000 Wh unit lasts 11 to 12 hours](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket).
- Other sources are more conservative. [Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/) assumes a constant 260 W for a queen blanket. At that draw, a generic 1,000 Wh unit lasts only about 3 hours. Your blanket's wattage and heat setting matter a lot, so check the label on your blanket.

**Other options**
- **BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, $449):** [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night) says it runs one 120 V blanket all night, or two on low. The AC inverter itself draws about 15 W. That page also says it's back in stock in late November, so it may not be available yet.
- **EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W):** [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy) lists a bundle with a 45W solar panel at $479 (was $598) at Best Buy. TechRadar hasn't tested this model. The 45W panel is too small to recharge it quickly, and the unit weighs 26.7 lb.
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2:** Blackout Wise says it covers about 23 hours for the same blanket. Choose it if you want two nights between charges.
- **If you want a larger margin for a high-wattage queen blanket:** Home Power Facts says a constant 260 W for 8 hours needs about 2,600 Wh. The lowest-priced unit it lists that can do this is the Jackery HomePower 3000 ($1,499 list, about 9.5 hours).

**What to skip**
- **300 Wh units are too small:** Blackout Wise says they run a 150 W blanket for only about 3 to 3.5 hours.
- **Even the 499 Wh Yeti 500 falls short:** it reaches about 5.5 hours.

**Tips**
- Plug the blanket straight into the station. Sunbeam's manuals say not to use extension cords or power strips, per Dealectric.
- Keep the station off the bed and away from the blanket's folds.
- Use a low setting to stretch the runtime.

**My pick:** the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 for one night. I didn't find a buy link for it in the results, so check current pricing with the retailer.
